$comment: Chain claims-sibling convention as in del-mh-001: `chain_claims` is a parallel array of decoded-claims objects for the `chain` placeholder entries; `chain_hash` is __COMPUTED_CHAIN_HASH__ (minter computes the correct §5 commitment — every signature and the hash are valid so the scope check is the isolated failure).
description: Multi-hop scope inflation (aitp/0.2 shape). chain[0] (B→C) declares scope ["read_data","admin"], but the voucher embedded in chain[0] (A→B) granted only ["read_data","write_data"]. The adjacent-pair scope rule (RFC-AITP-0011 §4) requires chain[0].scope ⊆ chain[0].voucher.grants; "admin" violates that at the voucher boundary. Every hop's JWS and the voucher are validly signed and chain_hash recomputes, and the OUTER pair check alone would pass (outer.scope [read_data] ⊆ chain[0].scope [read_data, admin]) — only checking every hop boundary, including the voucher boundary, catches the inflation. Verifier MUST reject with DELEGATION_SCOPE_EXCEEDED.

expected.rationale: chain[0].scope re-adds "admin", which is not in chain[0].voucher.grants ([read_data, write_data]). RFC-AITP-0011 §4 requires the subset relation at every hop boundary including the voucher boundary; checking only the most recent pair would not detect this.
